chapter: Fletcher Henderson and forming his own band
title: Substituting for Harvey Boone in Duke Ellington's band
summary: Carter recalls sitting in for Ellington's saxophonist at Harry Richman's club, an event Duke does not remember.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, let me go to another point. Now you're in New York, in and out of big bands, some of them your own, and the early thirties and coming up now, and you're about to form your first important band; let's

say important in jazz annals and important to you. What were your relations, let's say, by this time, let's say, with Duke? I mean Duke was around there -- did you know him intimately or fairly well? Did you run in to him, did you play for him now and then on occasion? Up until, say, the early thirties.

I cannot say that I knew him intimately, but at one point I do remember, and someone has told me that they spoke to Duke about this and Duke doesn't remember it, but I guess I was sort of a little insignificant as a musician around Harlem at the time -- he had a saxophone player with him named Harvey Boon, and Harvey Boon became ill and if my memory serves me properly, the Ellington band was at a club on 57th Street called Harry Richman's Club, and I sat in for Harvey Boon for a week or two -- I'm not sure what -- maybe it may have been a number of days, and it just felt like a week or two, you know, because playing with the great Ellington might have been just ...
We're continuing the discussion of your early relationship with Duke, and your recollection of playing with him, but his lack of recollection of that same event.
So as I was saying before we were so

rudely interrupted by the end of the tape on the other side, it might have been, you know, a few days or it might have been a couple of weeks -- but I do remember that I did sub for Harvey Boone in the Duke Ellington orchestra, and it might have been as early as 1926.
